Around the area are several buildings registered on the Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship Heritage List.


== Location ==
Kościelecki Square is located in the historical part of Old Bydgoszcz. It has a rectangular shape (200 metres (660 ft)×40 metres (130 ft)), with an east–west orientation, which central part is full of greenery. On the east, it is bordered by Bernardyńska Street, on the west by Przy Zamczysku street and its southern edge is lined up to the west with Długa street.
The main edifice in the area is Saint Andrew Bobola's Church, standing on the northern edge.
The southern side displays a frontage of buildings, among which the ancient Hospital for infants (German: Kleinkinder Klinik) at Nr.7, and the former school for girls (German: Erste Mädchen von Volkschule) both dating back from the beginning of the 20th century.
To the west is being constructed a modern business project, Immobile|K3.


== History ==
From the 11th to the 14th century, the area north of the square was occupied by a small city castle, destroyed in July 1330, by the Teutonic Knights.
